acceptance: A develop CI job or pr-preflight step fails when a test would fail or error on the curated release tree because it reads a stripped path.
The check uses the same curation commands as release-cut, read from one source, so the two cannot drift.
The release guide documents how to fix a failure: strip the test or skip it on the specific file it reads.
A dry run of release curation on current develop passes the CI fast selection, apart from known environment-only failures.
context:
Found during the v0.4.2 release. Release PR #2648 failed test with 12 failures and 31 errors, #2655 with 3 failures and 2 errors, both FileNotFoundError/ModuleNotFoundError on stripped paths. Related: dlv2-53-retire-legacy-release-path.

Closeout 2026-10-06 (owner kept the legacy release path for 0.4.3): PR #2733 merged to develop as d9872fb7d (mergedAt 2026-10-06T18:52:55Z, head 428ce8bab). Design: scripts/release_curation_dry_run.py reads the git rm commands from the release-cut recipe via check_release_curation.release_cut_rm_commands (the parser check_release_curation.py already used, now shared), applies them in a detached scratch worktree of HEAD, and runs pytest there with test.yml's marker selection. A step in ci.yml's code-test job runs it for each PR's changed test modules (a full fast run would add ~23 CI minutes); with no arguments it runs the full fast selection, which the release guide's new "Tests on the release tree" section asks for before a cut. The step is registered in the CI-local parity inventory (tests/system/test_ci_lint_parity.py, docs/operations/ci-local-parity.md). No Makefile change.

Acceptance: (1) the CI step fails a PR whose changed test fails on the curated tree; test_release_curation_dry_run.py shows the dry run fails on a newly added test that reads a removed path and passes on shipped paths. (2) one source: the check executes the git rm commands parsed from the release-cut recipe. (3) the release guide documents the fix (skip on the specific file, module pytestmark or importorskip, strip-list only for dev-only tooling). (4) full dry run on develop: the first run on 70c055227 found 6 real release-tree failures (test_api_reference_contract x2, test_uat_loc_bucket_coverage x3, test_corpus_cohort_depth import error), each now skipped when its specific development-only file is absent; the final full run on the branch passed 33,014 tests, 38 skipped, 0 failed. Required contexts core, docs, landing, explorer, results-data, tooling and oracle-review were SUCCESS on head 428ce8bab; oracle-review passed on a stand-in attestation that the agent posted at the owner's explicit instruction (provenance comment on the PR). Possible follow-up, not filed: a full dry run in release-canary.yml (its summary schema feeds readiness tooling). Worktree removed.
description: The release-cut target removes development-only paths (_project, AGENTS.md, .pre-commit-config.yaml and others) and a hand-maintained list of tests that read them. New tests that read those paths are not added to the list, so the next release PR fails its required test job and blocks release-required-result. v0.4.0, v0.4.1 and v0.4.2 each hit this; v0.4.2 needed two develop fixes (#2651, #2658) and three cuts. A local run of the CI fast selection on a simulated curated tree takes 3-5 minutes and found every remaining failure at once. Add a check on develop that applies the release curation to a scratch tree and runs collection or the fast test selection, or a static check that fails when a test outside the strip list references a stripped path. Prefer skipping individual tests on the specific file they read (the pattern used in #2658) over stripping whole files that mostly test shipped code.
